title: Skip the post-commit StateInner tail-trim lock when no sessions were persisted
outcome: A successful metadata-only persistence tick with no persisted session IDs performs no StateInner acquisition for tail trimming, while nonempty trimming, write/fence acknowledgement, watermarks, failure restoration and scheduling remain unchanged. This bounded correction does not claim to explain all historical P1 stalls.
acceptance: The production post-commit tail-trim path returns without acquiring StateInner when persisted_session_ids is empty; a deterministic held-StateInner regression exercises that actual shared path and proves completion before releasing the held state lock, without sleeps or synthetic load.

For nonempty persisted_session_ids, existing trimming behavior and mutation-stamp/active-session guards remain intact; controls cover eligible versus active or newer-mutated records. Persistence commit/fence acknowledgement, watermarks, tombstone restoration, retries, budgets and deadlines are unchanged.

The exact input has focused passing regression evidence and the maintained full gate, plus independent read-only Codex and Claude review with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding; Kimi substitutes only for unavailable Claude with the observed refusal recorded. Independent acceptance precedes completion.

Notes distinguish the proven elimination of an unnecessary lock from unresolved nonempty bookkeeping/storage/holder attribution; the P1 parent is not completed or declared root-caused by this correction alone.
